subject: SIG follow-up: SAML/SCIM gap mapping & least-privilege attestation schedule
messages:
From: Sara Gonzalez <sara.gonzalez@graystone.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIG evidence: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - initial request

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team is working through the SIG and has a concentrated set of asks around access controls. Can you provide a consolidated mapping and evidence for the following items by EOD Oct 8?

- SSO / SAML: identity providers supported, SAML metadata, assertion validation practice, MFA enforcement points.
- SCIM: provisioning flow, attribute mappings, example provisioning logs for a recent user lifecycle.
- RBAC & least privilege: roles inventory, default permissions for each role, and any delegation rules.
- MFA: supported factors, enforcement options (per-route/per-role), and exception processes.

If you have an access-control matrix and any diagrams that make this easier for reviewers, please attach. If you need more time, tell us the earliest completion date.

Best,
Sara
Sara Gonzalez
Senior Security Manager — Graystone Labs

PS: CCing compliance@graystone.com for visibility.

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Gonzalez <sara.gonzalez@graystone.com>, compliance@graystone.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG evidence: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - planned delivery

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a consolidated SIG access package. Attaching an editable access matrix and a short runbook we’ll use to collect the artifacts: sig-access-matrix.xlsx (see attached).

Proposed plan (owners + ETA):
- SSO / SAML artifact set (metadata, IdP compatibility notes, assertion validation tests) — owner: soojin_lee — ETA: 2027-10-06 EOD
- SCIM provisioning logs + attribute mapping export — owner: karthik_iyer — ETA: 2027-10-06 EOD
- RBAC role inventory & least-privilege attestation statement — owner: marissa_cole (product security) — ETA: 2027-10-07 noon
- MFA capabilities summary and enforcement policies — owner: jonas_weber — ETA: 2027-10-06 EOD

Outstanding questions we need from Graystone to finalize artifacts:
1) Do you need environment-specific evidence (prod-only) or both prod/stage?
2) Any preferred format for attestation (signed PDF from an exec vs. internal statement)?

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: prepare role inventory export and draft attestation language.
- Karthik: pull last 30 days of SCIM provisioning logs, anonymize PII.
- Soojin: collate SAML metadata and current validation test outputs.

We’ll send the package as a single zip with a short index and a one-page summary. If Graystone confirms prod-only is fine, we’ll proceed on that basis.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Security Programs — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig-access-matrix.xlsx (editable)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SIG evidence: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - role inventory + next steps

Team —

I’ve exported the role inventory and started a least-privilege attestation draft (attached to this thread in the shared drive). Highlights and decisions needed:

- Role inventory: 28 roles included (system_admin, infra_engineer, model_ops, app_read, app_write, support_agent, billing, auditor, etc.). I added default permissions per role and the last-modified timestamp.
- Delegation: we allow scoped delegation for on-call escalation (limited to 2-hour temporary elevated access) — need to call this out as an exception in the attestation.
- Attestation language: product security leads must sign off; I propose Marissa + Head of Product sign the attestation PDF. If Graystone requires an exec-level signature (CISO), we can escalate.

Karthik — thanks for the SCIM logs export. Please confirm you anonymized email/user ids. Attachments I uploaded to the drive: saml-flow-diagram.png, scim-provisioning-logs.txt.

Jonas — I left a short note in the access matrix about MFA enforcement points and per-route options. If Graystone wants stricter wording around "enforced for all interactive sessions," we can make that explicit.

Proposed delivery: consolidated zip (index + docs + logs) shipped 2027-10-07 10:00 AM PT. If anyone foresees a blocker, flag now.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Drive links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1QxSigAccess
Attachments (uploaded): saml-flow-diagram.png, scim-provisioning-logs.txt

From: Sara Gonzalez <sara.gonzalez@graystone.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@graystone.com
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: SAML/SCIM gap mapping & least-privilege attestation schedule

Jonas / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the matrix. We reviewed the index and the diagrams — they’re helpful. A couple of small clarifications before we route to our compliance committee:

1) For the SCIM logs you provided, can you confirm the pipeline anonymization approach (hashed user IDs vs. redaction) so our auditors understand traceability?
2) In the attestation draft you noted a 2-hour delegation exception for on-call — our policy requires documented approval steps for any elevated access. Can you add a short paragraph explaining the approval flow (who approves, where it’s logged)?

If you can fold those into the package and send by EOD Oct 8, we’ll be able to complete our SIG review and move to the vendor approval step next week.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Gonzalez
Senior Security Manager — Graystone Labs

--
Graystone Compliance Team will expect the finalized zip and the attestation PDF signed by Marissa + Head of Product (or CISO if requested).
